gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-fauna-one: Open-mouthed and distinctive, Bellota Text draws its letters without any pen shading to steer the eye. But Fauna One handles the text itself, a serif given a generous e eye and shallow ascenders and descenders.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-kadwa: A classic, editorial serif voice with open-ended curves is what the text carries, under Bellota Text headings that skip stem-to-join contrast. Kadwa's larger-than-usual x-height keeps a full page of paragraphs feeling generous rather than cramped.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-noticia-text: Bellota Text draws strokes like a bent steel rod. Against it, Noticia Text, a text serif, lets big visible entrances lead into each curve while lowercase fills most of the letter height.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla reads refined and authoritative, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals. Beside this classic serif, Bellota Text keeps a moderate lowercase height, and that display-versus-serif gap is the quality that makes the pairing memorable.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-epilogue: Inviting and personal, Bonbon lays down thick, heavy-looking handwritten letters with open throats. Epilogue brings curvy, wire-like monoline strokes and stubby ascender tips, made for quick bursts of reading.
gen-gf-bonbon-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified and editorial, a serif whose strokes gently ebb and flow with sturdy hairlines. And Bonbon does inviting handwriting best, while Erode does steady text best, though not for very long paragraphs.
gen-gf-bonbon-general-sans: Bonbon is all heavy, friendly handwriting with open throats. General Sans does the other job best, filling the line with smooth, steady curves built for brief bits of reading.
gen-gf-bonbon-satoshi: Personal and inviting, Bonbon hands over thick, casual handwriting with open throats. Satoshi, a sans of uniform strokes and a soaring x-height, does the cleaner work and suits quick snippets better than pages.
gen-gf-bowlby-one-sc-fs-paquito: Distinctive, with Bowlby One SC pressing its squared-off, woodblock-high letters and pinched mouths into the headline. But Paquito, this classic serif, sits confident and approachable with caps and lowercase nearly level, though it wearies once paragraphs pile up.
gen-gf-bpmf-iansui-fs-neco: Bpmf Iansui writes in one steady, toothpaste-like line, with an open s and hand-drawn ease. And Neco, the text serif, swells mellowly from hairline to stem, better taken in modest helpings than endless pages.
